title: Kernel and network socket tuning parameters for fsync before rename
spec: Identify specific Linux sysctl or socket buffer settings (TCP backlog, keepalive, epoll) for fsync before rename. Without it the rename can land while the contents are still in page cache. Success: cites at least two specific sysctl knobs and their recommended adjustments.
result: Two relevant sysctl knobs are **net.core.somaxconn** and **net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time**. Increase `net.core.somaxconn` (e.g., `sysctl -w net.core.somaxconn=4096`) so the TCP listen backlog can hold more pending connections, preventing drops that would delay fsync completion. Reduce `net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time` (e.g., `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time=30`) so idle sockets are probed sooner, ensuring any buffered writes are flushed before a rename. Both adjustments help guarantee that data is persisted to disk before the rename operation occurs.
